title: Name-Change Petition
description: Sample legal-document definition for a name-change petition or court form packet.

jurisdiction.jurisdiction_notes: Placeholder jurisdiction used for sample structure only.

sources.source_notes: This sample uses a placeholder source ID from sample source metadata.

legal_rules.rule_notes: Legal-rule records have not been added yet. This sample should remain proposed.

structure.structure_notes: Court form structure, caption requirements, signature requirements, and attachments must come from reviewed court sources.

user_facts.fact_notes: The user must provide and confirm all document facts. Pro-One must not infer sensitive facts or fill required court fields without user input.

prohibited_assistance: Claim the petition is legally sufficient.
Choose legal strategy for the user.
drafting.drafting_notes: Until legal rules, form sources, and evaluation fixtures are added, assistance should stay limited to explanation, checklist, and review prompts.

prohibited_guidance: File the document for the user.
Tell the user notarization is or is not required without reviewed source support.
Make the final filing decision for the user.
filing_or_service.filing_or_service_notes: Filing, signature, notarization, and packet requirements must be source-backed and reviewed.

deadlines.deadline_notes: Any filing timing, notice timing, hearing timing, or follow-up deadline must be supported by reviewed sources.

privacy.data_minimization_notes: Ask only for facts needed to identify the document category and explain source-backed next steps.
privacy.privacy_notes: Users should be warned not to share unnecessary sensitive information.

escalation_triggers: The document involves a minor.
The user reports safety, domestic violence, immigration, or sealed-record concerns.
The user has an urgent hearing or court deadline.
The user is unsure which court or form applies.
refusal_triggers: The user asks Pro-One to invent facts.
The user asks Pro-One to hide information from the court.
The user asks Pro-One to guarantee court approval.
The user asks for advice about evading legal requirements.
required_warnings: This document help provides legal information, not legal advice.
The user should review current court instructions before filing.
The user should seek legal help for urgent, complex, sealed-record, safety-related, or minor-child issues.
safety.safety_notes: This document definition should stay proposed until source, rule, workflow, and evaluation coverage is stronger.

review.review_notes: Sample legal-document definition only. Not approved for production use.

success_criteria: The document help does not invent facts.
The document help does not claim legal sufficiency.
The document help does not guarantee approval.
The document help directs filing and deadline uncertainty to sources or human help.
The document help limits sensitive-data collection.
known_failure_modes: Generating a filing-ready document too early.
Treating placeholder sources as approved sources.
Providing legal advice instead of legal information.
evaluation.evaluation_notes: Evaluation fixtures should be added before this document type is supported.

title: Discovery Response
description: Sample legal-document definition for a civil discovery response, including responses to interrogatories, requests for production, or requests for admission.

jurisdiction.jurisdiction_notes: Placeholder jurisdiction used for sample structure only.

sources.source_notes: These are placeholder source IDs. Matching source metadata records would need to be added before support.

legal_rules.rule_notes: Legal-rule records have not been added yet. Discovery response support must remain proposed.

structure.structure_notes: Discovery response structure is jurisdiction-specific and may vary by request type.

user_facts.fact_notes: The user must provide or confirm each factual response. Pro-One must not decide objections, privilege, or admissions for the user.

prohibited_assistance: Draft final discovery responses for service.
Decide whether to admit or deny a request.
Tell the user to withhold documents without legal review.
drafting.drafting_notes: Discovery responses are high-risk because they involve deadlines, admissions, objections, evidence, sanctions, and privilege.

prohibited_guidance: Serve discovery responses for the user.
Calculate the response deadline without reviewed source support.
Tell the user that verification is or is not required without reviewed source support.
filing_or_service.filing_or_service_notes: Discovery responses may not be filed in some courts unless connected to a motion or order. Service rules must be source-backed.

deadlines.deadline_notes: Discovery deadlines can create waiver, sanctions, admission, or case-dispositive risks. Human review should be encouraged.

privacy.data_minimization_notes: Avoid asking for full discovery responses unless necessary for source-backed explanation. Encourage summaries and redaction where appropriate.
privacy.privacy_notes: Users should avoid pasting privileged, confidential, or highly sensitive material unless necessary.

escalation_triggers: The user has a discovery response deadline.
The request may require an admission or denial.
The request may involve privileged or confidential information.
The user is considering withholding documents.
The user has received a motion to compel or sanctions threat.
The user is unsure whether an objection applies.
refusal_triggers: The user asks Pro-One to invent discovery responses.
The user asks Pro-One to hide responsive documents.
The user asks Pro-One to make a privilege determination.
The user asks Pro-One to decide whether to admit or deny a request without user-provided facts.
The user asks for strategy on avoiding disclosure unlawfully.
required_warnings: This discovery help provides legal information, not legal advice.
Discovery responses can affect rights, obligations, evidence, sanctions, and admissions.
The user should seek legal help before serving discovery responses, especially if deadlines, objections, privilege, or sanctions are involved.
safety.safety_notes: Discovery response help should be tightly limited until legal-rule and risk schemas are added.

review.review_notes: Sample legal-document definition only. Not approved for production use.

success_criteria: The document help does not invent responses.
The document help does not choose objections.
The document help does not decide privilege.
The document help flags deadlines, admissions, sanctions, and privilege risks.
The document help directs high-risk issues to human help.
known_failure_modes: Creating final responses that look ready to serve.
Encouraging disclosure of privileged or sensitive information.
evaluation.evaluation_notes: Evaluation fixtures should include interrogatories, requests for production, requests for admission, and objection-heavy scenarios.

title: Subpoena Information
description: Sample legal-document definition for explaining subpoena-related documents and boundaries.

jurisdiction.jurisdiction_notes: Placeholder jurisdiction used for sample structure only.

sources.source_notes: These are placeholder source IDs. Matching source metadata records would need to be added before support.

legal_rules.rule_notes: Legal-rule records have not been added yet. Subpoena support must remain proposed.

structure.structure_notes: Subpoena rules vary by jurisdiction, issuing authority, recipient type, and whether testimony, documents, or both are requested.

user_facts.fact_notes: Subpoena issues may be urgent. Pro-One should avoid deciding validity, objections, or compliance obligations.

prohibited_assistance: Draft final objections to a subpoena.
Tell the user to ignore a subpoena.
Decide whether the user must comply.
drafting.drafting_notes: Subpoena support should focus on issue spotting, source-backed explanation, and escalation.

prohibited_guidance: Serve a subpoena for the user.
Guarantee that an objection or motion will succeed.
Calculate subpoena response deadlines without reviewed source support.
filing_or_service.filing_or_service_notes: Subpoena issuance, service, compliance, objection, and motion practice must be source-backed and reviewed.

deadlines.deadline_notes: Subpoena deadlines may be short and high-risk. Human review should be encouraged.

privacy.data_minimization_notes: Ask for only enough information to identify the subpoena type, dates, issuing authority, and safety concerns.
privacy.privacy_notes: Users should avoid sharing full subpoena attachments or sensitive records unless necessary.

escalation_triggers: The subpoena has a near deadline.
The subpoena demands testimony.
The subpoena requests privileged, confidential, medical, financial, employment, or business records.
The user is considering ignoring the subpoena.
The user wants to object, move to quash, or withhold documents.
refusal_triggers: The user asks Pro-One to tell them to ignore a subpoena.
The user asks Pro-One to decide whether service is valid.
The user asks Pro-One to draft final objections or a motion to quash.
The user asks Pro-One to help destroy, hide, or withhold evidence unlawfully.
required_warnings: This subpoena help provides legal information, not legal advice.
Subpoenas can involve urgent deadlines and serious consequences.
The user should seek legal help promptly if a subpoena has a deadline, requests sensitive material, or may require testimony.
safety.safety_notes: Subpoena support should be treated as high risk until more rule and evaluation coverage exists.

review.review_notes: Sample legal-document definition only. Not approved for production use.

success_criteria: The document help does not decide subpoena validity.
The document help does not tell the user to ignore a subpoena.
The document help flags urgent deadlines and sensitive records.
The document help directs high-risk issues to human help.
known_failure_modes: Encouraging disclosure of privileged or sensitive material.
Treating a subpoena as a routine form.
evaluation.evaluation_notes: Evaluation fixtures should test recipients, nonparties, production-only subpoenas, testimony subpoenas, and sensitive records.

title: Small-Business Demand Letter
description: Sample legal-document definition for a small-business demand letter or pre-suit settlement communication.

jurisdiction.jurisdiction_notes: Placeholder jurisdiction used for sample structure only.

sources.source_notes: These are placeholder source IDs. Matching source metadata records would need to be added before support.

legal_rules.rule_notes: Legal-rule records have not been added yet. Demand-letter support must remain proposed.

structure.structure_notes: Demand letters should be factual, professional, and based only on user-confirmed facts.

user_facts.fact_notes: The user must confirm all factual statements and requested relief before any draft language is used.

prohibited_assistance: Provide a legal opinion on liability.
Use abusive, deceptive, or harassing language.
drafting.drafting_notes: A user-confirmed draft may be appropriate when the user provides and confirms all facts and requested content, but the output should remain legal information and practical communication support.

prohibited_guidance: Send the letter for the user.
Guarantee that the recipient must respond.
Tell the user that a demand letter satisfies a legal prerequisite without reviewed source support.
filing_or_service.filing_or_service_notes: Sending, response timing, and pre-suit prerequisite issues may require source support or human review.

deadlines.deadline_notes: Any legal prerequisite, statute of limitations, response deadline, or filing deadline must be source-backed and reviewed.

privacy.data_minimization_notes: Ask for summaries and only the facts needed to draft a professional communication.
privacy.privacy_notes: Users should avoid including unnecessary account numbers, private identifiers, or confidential business details.

escalation_triggers: The dispute involves a large amount of money.
The user has received a lawsuit, subpoena, agency notice, or attorney letter.
The user wants to threaten criminal action.
The user asks about statutes of limitation or legal prerequisites.
The dispute involves regulated business activity.
refusal_triggers: The user asks Pro-One to include false statements.
The user asks Pro-One to threaten unlawful action.
The user asks Pro-One to harass or intimidate the recipient.
The user asks Pro-One to fabricate evidence or documents.
required_warnings: This document help provides legal information, not legal advice.
The user must review and confirm all facts before sending anything.
The user should seek legal help for high-value, urgent, regulated, or lawsuit-related disputes.
safety.safety_notes: Demand-letter assistance may be lower risk than court filings, but facts, tone, deadlines, and legal threats still require controls.

review.review_notes: Sample legal-document definition only. Not approved for production use.

success_criteria: The document help uses only user-confirmed facts.
The document help avoids unsupported legal threats.
The document help avoids harassment or abusive tone.
The document help flags legal prerequisites and deadlines for source review.
The document help tells the user to review before sending.
known_failure_modes: Inventing facts to strengthen the demand.
Missing lawsuit or deadline escalation triggers.
evaluation.evaluation_notes: Evaluation fixtures should test unpaid invoice disputes, contract disputes, refund demands, and inappropriate threat requests.
